root.name: Sicilian Defense: Double-Dutch Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 f5 3. exf5 Nh6

overview: Black answers 2.Nf3 with the Dutch-style 2...f5 and, after 3.exf5, plays 3...Nh6 to recapture on f5 and develop. White keeps an extra pawn and a sound centre if he develops carefully, so Black is playing for time and kingside pressure. It is a rare surprise rather than a theory line.

white_ideas.idea: Take f5 and play d4 or Nc3 and Be2 with an extra pawn and a lead in the centre.
Avoid early queen outings and wait for Black to over-extend.

black_ideas.idea: Recapture on f5 with the knight or ...d6 and ...Nxf5.
Use the e8-h5 diagonal and ...Qb6 or ...c4 ideas for activity.

typical_structures.structure: White e-pawn gone, Black f-pawn gone: an open f-file with an asymmetric centre.

character.notes: Black is a pawn down in a double-edged position where one inaccurate move loses quickly.

gambit.notes: Black's f-pawn is offered after 3.exf5 and White can simply keep it.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; Black's compensation is thin against careful development.

structure.notes: Sicilian c5 against e4 with the f-file semi-open after the exchange.

approach.notes: A Black surprise weapon that strong players seldom choose.

level.notes: Few moves to learn but dubious, so never Beginner.
